title: Spill oversized text output of read verbs to a file
action: Add a new module output_spill (register it in main.rs) and wrap the one call `router::try_native(&args, t0)` in main() with it, so every println! site is covered without editing them (per 41814204). The wrap engages only when ALL hold (per f0aa3d67): the argv is on one allowlist const in output_spill — first token status; cells list; decisions list; backlog list; knowledge context; knowledge search; or any argv carrying --help — and the argv carries no --json, stdout is not a terminal (std::io::IsTerminal), BEE_OUTPUT_FULL is not 1, and the repo config read with state::read_config_raw over the root from roots::resolve_roots_core(cwd) (use the work root) holds output_spill_bytes as a positive integer (per 8b0803c8; absent or 0 means no wrap). On Unix, flush stdout, dup fd 1, dup2 a fresh file at <work_root>/.bee/tmp/output/<verb-tokens-joined-by-dash>-<utc stamp YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ>.txt onto fd 1, run the verb, flush, restore fd 1 with dup2, then: at or under the threshold copy the file bytes to stdout unchanged and delete the file; above it print the leading whole lines that fit in two thirds of the threshold, then exactly one marker line `[bee] output spilled: <omitted> of <total> bytes omitted — full output: <relative path>`, then the trailing whole lines that fit in one quarter of the threshold, and keep the file. Any failure to create the file or dup falls back to running the verb unwrapped. On Windows (cfg not unix) run the verb unwrapped. Return the verb's own ExitCode unchanged; stderr is never captured. No code comments of any kind (repo rule no_code_comments). Write integration tests in tests/output_spill.rs with assert_cmd against a tempfile fixture repo (write .bee/onboarding.json and .bee/config.json with output_spill_bytes) that run `bee --help --all`.

truths: With output_spill_bytes 8000 in the fixture config, `bee --help --all` stdout is at most 8000 bytes plus one marker line, contains `[bee] output spilled:` and a path under .bee/tmp/output/, and that file holds the full help text
Without output_spill_bytes, with BEE_OUTPUT_FULL=1, or with --json, the stdout bytes equal the unwrapped output and no file is written under .bee/tmp/output/
The exit code of a wrapped run equals the exit code of the same run unwrapped
